title: The Registry Has One Column: Theophrastus's Characters as a Named Authorial Function (v0.1)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: Theophrastus's Characters, read not as a minor genre-piece but as an operation visible on the page: each sketch runs one engine — a hedged definition (δόξειεν ἂν εἶναι, ὡς τύπῳ λαβεῖν), then τοιοῦτός τις, οἷος … and a καί-chain of infinitives — a disposition rendered as a registry of characteristic deeds with name, scene, verdict, and theory removed. Examined in four terms: on its own (a πίναξ of sorts; the descriptive register at its purest, γάρ 37 per ten thousand; the spurious prooemium as a received character of the author); in terms of Plato (the Republic's democratic man already a sketch inside an argument; the Apology's ἔστιν τις Σωκράτης grammatically a Character; the first Character, irony, Socrates's method by his enemies' name with ἀποροῦμαι among the ironist's stock evasions); in terms of Aristotle (the Ethics' objects shared, its scale absent — thirty vices, no mean: the registry has one column; the definition-hedge the treatise's own; EN IV 7 restoring the name, οἷον καὶ Σωκράτης ἐποίει; the oligarch's one Homeric line the line Λ 10 ends on); as the mediating term (dialogue → sketch → category; definition sought → stated → explained; person present → removed → restored as example — one trait traversing three named authorial functions). Then the test: the three modes stated as operations indexed by names, and the middle one measured on its proper control, Aristotle's own sketches of ἤθη in Rhetoric II — the same genre under the other name explains where the Characters enumerate (γάρ 259 vs 37; cause-demand 3.02 vs 0.74 per thousand) and names where they mark sorts (τις/τοιοῦτος 9.0 vs 16.4). Two earlier supports are retracted on the same run (the descriptive/explanatory register recurs within each name at equal magnitude; the Ethics' frame vocabulary is EN-specific). Nothing about dates, hands, or membership. Extracted from the notebook The First Draft (§§11, 13); companion to Aristotelian or Theophrastan (#1583) and Beautiful and New (#1579).

wiki_article: "The Registry Has One Column: Theophrastus's Characters as a Named Authorial Function" is a paper by Lee Sharks (v0.1, 6 September 2026) that reads the Characters as an operation rather than a genre. Each of the thirty sketches runs one engine: a hedged definition in the treatise's own manner, then τοιοῦτός τις, οἷος … and a καί-chain of infinitives — a disposition rendered as a registry of characteristic deeds with name, scene, verdict and theory removed. Examined on its own terms, the book is a πίναξ of sorts in the purest measured descriptive register; in terms of Plato, it keeps the sorts Athens is made of (the Republic's democratic man is already a sketch inside an argument; the Apology's ἔστιν τις Σωκράτης is grammatically a Character) and strips the drama; in terms of Aristotle, it shares the Ethics' objects and lacks its scale — thirty vices, no mean, no virtue: the registry has one column — while EN IV 7 restores the name the sketch removed (οἷον καὶ Σωκράτης ἐποίει). One trait, irony, runs the whole line — Socrates's method in Plato, an anonymous vice with ἀποροῦμαι among its stock evasions in the Characters, the deficiency about truth in the Ethics — and so traverses three named authorial functions: person, sort, example. The paper states the three modes as operations indexed by names (dramatize; extract, classify, register; organize, explain) and tests the middle one on its proper control, Aristotle's own sketches of ἤθη in Rhetoric II: the same genre under the other name explains where the Characters enumerate (γάρ 259 against 37 per ten thousand; cause-demand 3.02 against 0.74 per thousand) and names where they mark sorts (τις/τοιοῦτος 9.0 against 16.4). Two earlier supports are retracted on the same run: the descriptive/explanatory register recurs within each name at equal magnitude, and the Ethics' frame vocabulary is EN-specific. Nothing about dates, hands, or membership is asserted. Extracted from the notebook The First Draft; companion to Aristotelian or Theophrastan (#1583) and Beautiful and New (#1579).

defines_concepts.definition: An operation indexed by an author-name and capable of recurring — dramatize; extract, classify, register; organize, explain — read from a corpus's own divisions rather than from persons, and measured against the same genre under another name.
The state of a field of objects shared with a theory but carried without the theory's scale: the Characters' thirty vices with no mean, no virtue, and no axis — a registry, not an architecture.
